outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the upper bound on the constant c = lim M(n)/n has been lowered repeatedly, from 0.380926 (Haugland, 2016) to 0.380924 (AlphaEvolve, June 2025), 0.380876 (TTT-Discover, January 2026), 0.380874 (Aster, February 2026), 0.380868 (SimpleTES, April 2026; its text also gives 0.380856), 0.380871 (EinsteinArena/Together AI, by April 2026), 0.3808586 (EinsteinArena leaderboard, dated 15 August 2026 by a forum comment) and 0.3808568 (MILO, September 2026); the lower bound has risen from 0.379005 (White, 2022) to 0.37912 (Kim and Pilanci, June 2026) and to about 0.38056 via GitHub computer-assisted certificates (29 June to 14 September 2026, the first credited in a forum post to 'GPT Pro'), none yet refereed; the constant itself is not determined.
problem_asks: (1) For each n, M(n) is the minimum, over all splittings of {1, ..., 2n} into two sets A and B with |A| = |B| = n, of the largest number of solutions to a - b = k with a in A and b in B, taken over all integers k. (2) Estimate M(n) for large n: in the form the standard reformulation takes (Erdos problem 36), find or bound the optimal constant c = lim M(n)/n, i.e. give an upper and a lower bound on c, or determine c. The statement asks for an estimate, not an exact value. Per the sources, the existence of the limit was proved by Haugland using a Swinnerton-Dyer reduction to an infimum over step functions; the open part is the value of c and therefore the bounds on it. No other sub-question is listed in the statement.

events.what_happened: Leo Moser gives the lower bound sqrt(4 - sqrt(15)) = 0.356393 for the constant (listed in the Wikipedia table, year 1959; the paper itself, Acta Arithmetica 5 (1959) 117-119, was not opened).
events.remains: The upper bound and the exact value of c.

events.what_happened: J. K. Haugland, Journal of Number Theory 58 (1996) 71-78, gives an upper bound 0.382002 from a 21-step function, using Swinnerton-Dyer's reduction of the limit to an infimum over step functions. The 1996 paper itself was not opened; the value and the reduction are taken from the Wikipedia table (opened) and Haugland's 2016 note (opened). Tao's optimization-problems table also lists an unpublished Haugland value of 0.385694 from 1993.
events.remains: The lower bound and the exact value of c.
events.object: A 21-step function giving the value 0.382002 (per Haugland 2016's description). Explicit, numerical.

events.what_happened: J. K. Haugland, 'The minimum overlap problem revisited', arXiv:1609.08000 (single version, submitted 23 September 2016). The abstract says: 'A step function that improves the upper bound from 0.382002... to 0.380926... is given.' Tao's table and the Wikipedia table list 0.380926 for this paper. The AlphaEvolve paper calls the previous record 0.380927, a small discrepancy between sources.
events.revisions: v1 only, 23 Sep 2016 (arXiv listing). No journal reference listed on the arXiv page.
events.remains: The lower bound (0.379005 by White 2022) and the exact value of c.
events.directly_checkable: The step function is described in the note; the note does not list the function's values in the abstract I read.
events.direction: Upper bound; moved the upper bound down slightly. Cited as the prior record by AlphaEvolve and by TTT-Discover.
events.object: A step function (number of steps stated as 51 on Haugland's project page, not read) giving the overlap value 0.380926. Explicit, numerical.

events.what_happened: Ethan Patrick White, 'Erdos' minimum overlap problem', arXiv:2201.05704 (single version, submitted 14 January 2022): abstract says 'We obtain a substantially improved lower bound for the minimum overlap problem asked by Erdos.' Method: elementary Fourier analysis reducing the problem to a convex optimisation program; main result lim M(n)/n > 0.379005. The arXiv page gives no journal reference; the Acta Arithmetica 208 (2023) 235-255 publication was taken from search metadata and not opened.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv (14 Jan 2022). Journal version: Acta Arithmetica 208 (2023) 235-255, per search metadata.
events.delivers: Lower bound c >= 0.379005. The only lower bound in the published literature before the 2026 claims below.
events.remains: The upper bound beyond the step-function records, and the exact value of c.

events.what_happened: AlphaEvolve (Novikov et al., Google DeepMind), arXiv:2506.13131, reports an upper bound C5 <= 0.380924 for the minimum-overlap constant. Section 3.2 lists it among combinatorics and number theory results, saying AlphaEvolve 'established a new upper bound for the minimum overlap problem'. Appendix B.5 gives the definition, the previous bound (0.379005 <= C5 <= 0.380927, the upper bound attributed to Haugland 2016) and says the new value 'does ever so slightly better than the previous bound'. The construction is a step function found by an LLM-driven evolutionary search program.
events.revisions: v1 submitted 16 Jun 2025; the version I opened (v1 html) contains Appendix B.5. Later versions were not checked.
events.delivers: Upper bound c <= 0.380924, moving the record down by about 3 x 10^-6. Restriction: a numerical step-function value; the paper does not give the step-function coefficients in the text I read.

events.directly_checkable: A piecewise-constant step function whose overlap value is a finite computation. Its coefficients were not located in the text I read, so I did not check it.
events.doubts: No independent verification of the AlphaEvolve function found. Tao's forum post of 12 Jan 2026 reports the improvement ('could improve the upper bound very slightly to 0.380924') without describing any check. events.direction: Upper bound lowered; does not contradict any assertion of the statement. The problem asks for an estimate, and this event improves one side of it.
events.object: A step function on [0,2] with values in [0,1] and integral 1 whose maximal shifted overlap is 0.380924 (as claimed). Explicit (numerical), not an existence proof. Per the Haugland/Swinnerton-Dyer reduction it gives an upper bound on c.

events.what_happened: Sungyoon Kim and Mert Pilanci (Stanford Electrical Engineering), 'AI-Assisted Discovery of Convex Relaxations via Dual Agents', arXiv:2606.31182 (v1 30 Jun 2026). Starting from White's convex program, a coding agent proposes valid tightening constraints and a theory agent verifies each and searches for counterexamples; the paper's abstract reports certified lower bounds 'from 0.379005 to 0.37912' for the minimum-overlap constant (C6.5). Each bound is certified by an explicit dual-feasible point checked in rigorous interval arithmetic. The same work appeared as a poster at the 3rd AI for Math Workshop at ICML 2026 (11 Jul 2026), under the title 'Dual-Agent Convex Relaxation: Sharper Bounds for Two Autocorrelation Inequalities'. The ICML page does not say main-conference acceptance.
events.revisions: v1 30 Jun 2026 (the only version I checked).
events.delivers: Lower bound c >= 0.37912 (from 0.379005). Restriction: a bound derived from White's convex program with extra constraints found by the agent loop; no upper bound change. Weaker than the 0.38055 lower-bound certificates posted from 29 June 2026 (see the Price event).
events.remains: The exact value of c and the upper bound.

The README claims c > 0.38055470 from a computer-assisted proof: an Arb/python-flint ball-arithmetic verifier (prove_erdos_0380554275_arb.py) run at target 0.38055470 over all 172 mean bins, reporting proved_all_bins true and worst_bin_index 85, with an inverse worst-case D upper bound of 0.3805547027626 and a margin of about 1.9 x 10^-8. disputes.summary: Three GitHub claims in June to September 2026 move the lower bound for the same constant: Price's 0.38055470 (29 Jun 2026), emerardd's 0.380557 (3 Sep) and 0.38056070 (7 Sep), and ruturajr-raval's 0.38055925 (4 Sep). emerardd and ruturajr-raval both reuse Price's 170 noncentral Arb balls and replace the two central bins. Kim and Pilanci's 0.37912 (30 Jun 2026) is weaker than all of them. None is refereed; the record does not settle which claim the constant's status rests on.

The AI credit for the 0.38055470 lower bound is disputed between sources: the forum post says 'GPT Pro', the teorth AI-contributions wiki says 'GPT-5.5 Pro' (dated 29 Jun 2026, 'Candidate partial result'), and the GitHub repository names no model at all.

The 0.380924 upper bound is credited to 'AlphaEvolve (Novikov et al.)' in Wikipedia's table and the Tao optimisation table, to 'AlphaEvolve [Novikov et al. (2025)]; [Georgiev et al. (2025)]' in the TTT-Discover paper, and to 'AlphaEvolve (0.380924, Gemini-2.0 Pro)' in the SimpleTES blog. The model string appears only in third-party sources, not in the AlphaEvolve text read.

SimpleTES's Erdos value is 0.380868 in Table 1, Section 3.4.1, Figure 6 and the blog, but 0.380856 in the v1 introduction and in a 30 Apr 2026 forum citation; Section 4.4.1 describes 0.380856 as an ablation result excluded from the table. A later forum comment calls 0.380856 a typo. Unresolved.

The erdosproblems.com history page dates an entry to 2025-10-20 whose text credits the 0.38092876 upper bound to 'the TTT-Discover LLM' (a 2026 paper). The date cannot be the date of that attribution, so the history dating is unreliable; the tracker's AlphaEvolve row is dated 3 Nov 2025.

summary: Since January 2024 the Erdos minimum-overlap constant c = lim M(n)/n has moved on both sides, and every move after mid-2025 that I found is a numerical or computer-assisted bound, with AI systems credited for most of the upper-bound steps and for one lower-bound step. On the upper side: AlphaEvolve's 0.380924 (arXiv 2506.13131 v1, 16 Jun 2025; Section 3.2 and Appendix B.5) improves Haugland's 0.380926 (2016) by about 3 x 10^-6; the appendix states no piece count, and the 95-piece figure in TTT-Discover's caption is unverified. TTT-Discover (arXiv 2601.16175 v1, 22 Jan 2026; open model OpenAI gpt-oss-120b) reaches 0.380876 with a 600-piece asymmetric step function, and its Section 4.1.4 names Prof. Davide Torlo, a numerical-analysis researcher, who says the functions 'give bounds that improve upon the state of the art'. That is the only human check of a post-2025 upper-bound construction I found, and it checks the arithmetic of the functions rather than the reduction from c to step functions. Aster (arXiv 2602.07040, 3 Feb 2026) reports 0.380874 with 8192 pieces, naming no model for the run. SimpleTES (arXiv 2604.19341, 21 Apr 2026; gpt-oss-120b) reports 0.380868 in its table and text, but its v1 introduction and an ablation give 0.380856, which I could not reconcile; an automated AI referee (Pith) objects that the SOTA claims rest on unvalidated problem-specific scorers. Together AI's EinsteinArena entry (0.380871, by April 2026) is an arena result with no paper, and the arena's later entries (CodexProLong 0.3808586, dated 15 Aug 2026 only by a forum comment; MILO 0.3808568, arXiv 2609.38349, 29 Sep 2026) name no model for the constructions. On the lower side: White's 0.379005 (arXiv 2022, Acta Arithmetica 2023) stood until Kim and Pilanci (arXiv 2606.31182, 30 Jun 2026; 'We used Claude Opus 4.6 for our agent experiments') certified 0.37912 via an agent loop that adds constraints to White's convex program; their work was a workshop poster at the ICML 2026 AI for Math Workshop (11 Jul 2026). On 29 Jun 2026 Liam Price posted a computer-assisted certificate of c > 0.38055470 on the Erdos forum with the words 'GPT Pro improves the lower bound to 0.38055470'; the GitHub README names no model, the optimizer is unidentified, and the teorth AI-contributions wiki records 'GPT-5.5 Pro' for that date as a 'Candidate partial result'. Two later GitHub packages build on Price's 170 noncentral Arb balls: ruturajr-raval (v0.2.0, 4 Sep 2026, c_E > 0.38055925) and emerardd (v1.0.0-v1.1.1, 3 to 14 Sep 2026, c_E > 0.38056070, with a Zenodo record whose creator is listed as 'Deng, Haowen'; the link between that name and the GitHub account is not confirmed). None of the lower-bound certificates is refereed; emerardd's README says its centre verifier 'is not a third-party audit', and ruturajr-raval says 'independent external mathematical review' is not claimed. I did not run any certificate. The erdosproblems.com copy I could open is dated 23 January 2026 and still lists 0.379005 < c < 0.380876, so the live page may differ. Close calls: whether a GitHub certificate with no author-stated AI role should move the lower bound is for the later pass; whether 'GPT Pro' was load-bearing is unknown; and whether the 0.380856 or 0.380868 SimpleTES value stands. Pre-window history is recorded as events (Moser 1959, Haugland 1996 and 2016, White 2022); Erdos's 1955 conjecture c = 1/2 was overtaken by Motzkin, Ralston and Selfridge's 2/5 bound in 1956 (per Tao's table). Dead ends: no 'Zhao 2023' lower bound exists (the searches returned only White); the Cloninger-Steinerberger autoconvolution results are a different constant; OpenAI's May 2026 unit-distance result, Gemini Deep Think/Aletheia results, and Anthropic/Claude searches do not touch this constant; the AlphaEvolve repository page for problem 5 is an empty template; the Quanta article of 3 Aug 2026 does not mention the problem, though it mentions Liam Price on Erdos problem 1196.
competing_reading: Read strictly, no lower bound in the window comes from a qualified, public, refereed source: White's 0.379005 (2022) remains the only peer-reviewed lower bound, Kim and Pilanci's 0.37912 is a workshop poster, and the 0.38055 to 0.38056 values are unrefereed GitHub certificates whose only AI credit is a forum post, so they should not move the lower bound at all. Read broadly, the constant has been squeezed from 0.379005-0.380926 to roughly 0.380556-0.380857 (a gap of about 3 x 10^-4) within six months, with AI systems credited for every upper-bound step after June 2025 and for the one lower-bound step that rests on a human-run certificate. On the upper bound, a strict reading would count only the human-reviewed TTT-Discover value, and even that review checks arithmetic, not the reduction.
what_would_settle_it: For the lower bound: a posting of Price's certificate or the emerardd/ruturajr-raval certificates with named authors and the identity of the optimizer; an exact-rational or independent recomputation of the 0.38055470 and 0.38056070 values; and a statement by Price on which model produced the centre-bin certificate. For the upper bound: AlphaEvolve's step-function coefficients, to confirm 0.380924 and the piece count; SimpleTES's code or Section 4.4.1, to settle 0.380856 against 0.380868; and the arena's dated leaderboard history, to date the 0.380871 and 0.3808586 entries. For AI credit on the arena entries: a statement from the operators naming the model. For the record itself: the current erdosproblems.com/36 page, Tao's optimisation table, and the 2606.10402 table, to see whether any of these have been updated.

event.what_happened: AlphaEvolve (Novikov et al., Google DeepMind), arXiv:2506.13131, reports an upper bound C5 <= 0.380924 for the minimum-overlap constant. Section 3.2 lists it among combinatorics and number theory results, saying AlphaEvolve 'established a new upper bound for the minimum overlap problem'. Appendix B.5 gives the definition, the previous bound (0.379005 <= C5 <= 0.380927, the upper bound attributed to Haugland 2016) and says the new value 'does ever so slightly better than the previous bound'. The construction is a step function found by an LLM-driven evolutionary search program.
event.revisions: v1 submitted 16 Jun 2025; the version I opened (v1 html) contains Appendix B.5. Later versions were not checked.
event.delivers: Upper bound c <= 0.380924, moving the record down by about 3 x 10^-6. Restriction: a numerical step-function value; the paper does not give the step-function coefficients in the text I read.
event.remains: The exact value of c; the lower bound (0.379005 at the time).
event.time_since_posted: about 16 months, with no independent check of AlphaEvolve's step function located
event.directly_checkable: A piecewise-constant step function whose overlap value is a finite computation. Its coefficients were not located in the text I read, so I did not check it.
event.doubts: No independent verification of the AlphaEvolve function found. Tao's forum post of 12 Jan 2026 reports the improvement ('could improve the upper bound very slightly to 0.380924') without describing any check. TTT-Discover's Figure 2 caption calls AlphaEvolve's construction '95-piece' and describes it as symmetric; the 95-piece count is not stated in the AlphaEvolve Appendix B.5 text I read, so it is unverified here.
event.direction: Upper bound lowered; does not contradict any assertion of the statement. The problem asks for an estimate, and this event improves one side of it.
event.object: A step function on [0,2] with values in [0,1] and integral 1 whose maximal shifted overlap is 0.380924 (as claimed). Explicit (numerical), not an existence proof. Per the Haugland/Swinnerton-Dyer reduction it gives an upper bound on c.

The model is not named in Appendix B.5 (which says only 'AlphaEvolve'). A third-party source, the SimpleTES blog (June 2026), names 'Gemini-2.0 Pro' for this result; that model string is not from the AlphaEvolve text.

judgement.why: The statement asks for an estimate of the constant c = lim M(n)/n, and nothing in the record determines it, so every substantive event is a bound on one side. The 2025-26 step functions (AlphaEvolve, TTT-Discover, Aster, SimpleTES, arena entries, MILO) lower the upper bound; Kim-Pilanci and the Price/emerardd/ruturajr-raval certificates raise the lower bound. TTT-Discover is marked checkable because its explicit, released step function was checked numerically by a named reviewer (Torlo). That check covers the arithmetic, which is the whole of the claim once the standard reduction is accepted. Other step functions were not located, so they stay unreviewed. The machine-checked lower-bound certificates are large interval-arithmetic computations, too big to count as simple checks, so they are unreviewed. AI roles: AlphaEvolve, TTT-Discover, Aster, SimpleTES and MILO are credited as the producers of the constructions, so generated. Kim-Pilanci is assisted: a human-designed convex program plus constraints the agent found. Price's certificate is generated on the poster's own words, though no model is named in the repo. The arena entries have no systems recorded, so none. The Georgiev-Tao paper restates an earlier bound, so scope none. The GCL small-n enumeration is instances.
judgement.doubts: The AI credit for Price's 0.38055470 rests only on a forum post ('GPT Pro'); if that is wrong, the lower-bound AI role would drop. Together AI's 'internal agents' and CodexProLong were plausibly AI, but no system was recorded, so they are scored none. All quotes came through a summarising fetch tool.
judgement.by: judging pass (JUDGE.md), claude-opus-5-5; not the researching agent and not a human reviewer
